judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single expiry sentence; the bracketed editorial gloss and the date are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It declares 21-B.1 to 21-B.3 dead as of 1975 while they remain printed in the 1981–84 book, and the closing memorandum continues every side agreement 'deemed updated' — an unresolved contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger '75, 60, 50, 40 or fewer copies per load' is an odd descending list that reads as though several thresholds were merged, and 'extra roto or rotos' is loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grants overtime to four named individuals, which sits against 5-M's unfair-distribution rule and 8-C's non-discrimination principle but does not squarely conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise load cap with a stated exception for pallet trucks.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D's Newspoint schedules set different maxima and 3-A.2 requires each Publisher to publish its own load schedule; the relationship between the general and shop-specific caps is arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A grab-bag of eight lettered items of varying definiteness; (b)'s 'no reduction in the present number of a.m. routes' with a stated count and (g)'s 'except as provided in the Newspoint Agreement' are the softest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item (g)'s tailman rule at 180 loads conflicts with the 21-D Newspoint schedules unless the express carve-out is applied, and 3-D.1 recognises the right to reduce routes that (b) freezes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Transport men hired according to need' is a fragment with no subject or standard — its meaning is essentially indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on manning obligations elsewhere (21-D.III, 4-A.2 hiring) but is too thin to conflict with anything specific.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The table is internally inconsistent as printed: '45 papers' appears between 100 and 50, and the final line says tailmen will be employed on all Schedule A runs although the column is headed 'without tailmen'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedules B and C set higher no-tailman maxima with an asterisk reverting to Schedule A, and 21-C.3(g) sets a 180-load tailman trigger; harmonising the four is genuinely difficult.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean table, though the asterisk in its column heading is defined only under Schedule C.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The asterisked reversion rule appears in 21-D.I.C and applies to this schedule too, which is only implicit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The footnote 'If these schedules are exceeded then Schedule A will apply' is circular, since Schedule A's caps are lower in some bands and higher in others.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reverting to Schedule A, which requires tailmen on all runs, is hard to reconcile with these franchise caps 'without a tailman'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of recovery runs plus a clear 100-load cap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A excludes recovery runs from its tailman requirement, consistent with this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Present practice with respect to running time' incorporates an undocumented practice with no benchmark.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D(ix) fixes a mileage-based run-time rule for The Times, showing the parties knew how to specify run time when they wished; no direct conflict for The News.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat 250-load maximum; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-C.2 caps News trucks at 240 loads at 148 or more pages, which is a lower figure for a partly overlapping situation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Present practice will be continued' has no ascertainable content on the face of the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leaves pallet-truck loading outside the schedules in 21-D.I and 21-C.2, which is a gap rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '8 general floormen to be used when and where needed as directed' and the heading '(Day side, double out only)' leave the manning obligation's scope uncertain, and loaders may be 'rotated' yet must be present at the positions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A Times supplementary agreement fixes different floor-hire minima at Carlstadt and 22-A sets Times manning; for The News, 21-D.VIII's supersession clause governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear breaks with a stated compensation route, although the text is OCR-damaged ('pre-ided', 'mvening').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It compensates worked breaks 'as provided in Section 5N', but 5-N provides half an hour at time and one-half for a worked lunch, not for coffee breaks — an imperfect fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In line with current policy' and the phrase 'contractually designated territorial coverage' leave the delivery points for outside work largely at The News's discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph (c) expressly disapplies 3-L's extra-crew requirement at Newspoint, an acknowledged conflict resolved by carve-out; Section 1 supplies the territorial definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause promises continued day-side employment for 58 named men and then disclaims that it is 'a guaranty of 58 day jobs' — the two sentences pull against each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the Union's right to argue vacated jobs stay on the day side, which cuts against 3-D.1's rearrangement rights and 3-I's shift discretion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short cross-reference to Section 4 posting; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4-B's posting and bidding procedure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Supersedes and replaces all other agreements, memoranda or practices which would otherwise relate or be applicable ... except as otherwise stated herein' is a broad supersession with a vague saving clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The closing memorandum continuing 'every memorandum, letter agreement or side agreement' and 21-C.3's franchise items both bear on Newspoint, so what survives supersession is genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of unrelated understandings, including 'The IBM stipulation continues' (an undefined external document) and 'reviewed and revised in a fair and equitable manner'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The one-week notice of changes in method of delivery overlaps 5-J's four-day notice and 16-M.3's consent requirement without stating how they interact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is anchored to 'the calendar year 1966' and 'the plan as amended in paragraph 2 below', a fifteen-year-old benchmark carried forward with no updating.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates a separate arbitration channel (actuaries and a third actuary) that bypasses Section 16, and 21-F.3 routes disputes back to that paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare instruction to select one of two options with no deadline and no default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Options (a) and (b) are alternatives yet (b) is expressly built on (a)'s amendments, so the 'one option' choice is not clean.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Advance written approval of the chapel and advance written approval of the Union' for any plan change is a sweeping veto, and dates from 1964/1970 are stale.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It concerns The News's own plan while 13-I governs the joint Pension Fund, so two pension regimes coexist for the same employees without a stated priority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Benefits shall be provided under a new pension plan, the terms of which shall be jointly agreed upon' is an agreement to agree with no fallback.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 2(a) although it is presented as an alternative to it, and it leaves post-1970 benefits undetermined while 13-I requires contributions to the joint Fund.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is ungrammatical ('In the event that it is mutually agreed that a pension agreement already negotiated ... or there is a pension agreement which is negotiated'), and 'taken in their entirety, more favorable' is a vague comparison test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A 1981 side letter contains a broader most-favoured-organisation promise on pension, welfare and insurance, so two differently worded favoured-nation clauses coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure recital of what the parties 'acknowledged' and 'recognize'; it creates no obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a recital preceding 21-G.2's operative bar on unilateral implementation, and the efficiency recital points the opposite way from the consent requirement — a recital-versus-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such concept shall not be put into effect without agreement of the NMDU' is an absolute veto stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against 3-B and 3-D.1's management rights over routes and against the 21-G.1 recital of the need for efficiency; 16-M.3's consent rule is its general analogue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short expiry statement with bracketed editorial supplementation of both the period and the start date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Three years from March 31, 1981' would end March 31, 1984 whereas Section 19 ends the Agreement March 30, 1984 — a one-day mismatch, and the final memorandum continues side agreements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Largely recital and commitment language — 'maximum productivity and efficiency', 'undue hardships', 'manning that is necessary' — with no operative standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The commitment to maximum productivity and the preservation of the Union's right to negotiate manning point in opposite directions, and the affirmation of resolution 'without interruption of operations' overlaps 16-N.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The passage is severely garbled with marginal notes interleaved, so the offloading and Sta-Hi sentences run into each other and the 'In addition to that: prior to the start each week' clause is broken.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Sta-Hi sentence duplicates the separate 'Sta-Hi Newstrack & Truck Loaders' entry, which itself begins mid-sentence — the two fragments plainly belong together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise physical definition of where an insert tying line begins and ends.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Word-for-word parallel to the press tying line definition; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or percentage equivalent of the city circulation which is approximately 4' is incomplete — the figure is plainly corrupted and the alternative measure is unusable as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel PTL city-delivery entry uses the same 'or percentage equivalent of city circulation' formula without a figure at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short exclusive-jurisdiction statement over a defined product; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the surrounding ITL entries and 2-A/2-C jurisdiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite, though 'city completes' is an undefined trade term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the combo-run and four-sheet entries.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise definition mirroring the ITL definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent throughout the Carlstadt minutes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or percentage equivalent of city circulation' offers an alternative measure with no percentage stated, leaving the entitlement unquantified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The combo-run ITL entry uses the same formula with a corrupted figure; neither supplies a usable number.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision as reproduced begins mid-sentence ('truck loaders, including, but not limited to, operations, control and clearing of jams') with no subject or verb.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its missing opening sentence appears interleaved in the Offloading entry, so the two provisions as split are mutually incomplete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear physical boundary for jurisdiction over a named machine.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other jurisdictional boundary statements in these minutes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and absolute; 'handling of tied bundles' is broad but the subject matter is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the ITL/PTL boundaries which end at the bundle injector, so where 'handling' begins is a possible seam.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or any other operation under the jurisdiction of the delivery department' is a circular catch-all, since jurisdiction is what the clause is defining.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires console personnel to be Journeymen 'not supervisors', which sits against 6-A.1 vesting authority in the foreman and 6-E's exclusive power to change operating procedures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete list of tasks for a defined product line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-C.3(c) assigns odds make-up to home delivery routemen at The News; the two shops are separately regulated so no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A residual clause preserving 'any operations over which the delivery department had jurisdiction at 43d Street, whether by contract or by precedent' — a general catch-all resting on unrecorded precedent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against the specific enumerated jurisdictions in these minutes (expressio unius) and against 2-H.1's freeze of other unions' mailroom jurisdiction at a different plant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Under any and all operating conditions a minimum of one' is emphatic and precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A Times supplementary agreement adds a utility man and fixes combined floor hires at eighty-one, which is a different manning commitment for the same plant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Two 165-minute coffee breaks or one 80-minute coffee break' is obviously corrupted (15 and 30 minutes were surely intended), and the corruption goes to the entitlement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-N's paid-lunch rule and 22-C(d)'s relief periods cover the same ground with different figures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '80 minutes for lunch' is likewise almost certainly a corruption of 30 minutes, and 'as the office may direct' is loosely placed within the relief formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-C(d) states the same relief periods (20 minutes per trailer, 15 per suburban or mail bag truck), so the two provisions duplicate each other with 22-C(e) sending disputes to a named individual.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deadlines of 1976–77 measured from 'ratification of this Agreement' in a 1981 book, and 'a location 150 miles from Columbus Circle' without saying at least or at most.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D(iii) requires transfer points 'more than 150 miles' for long runs while (iv) requires 'no farther than 150 miles' for multi-stop runs, so the bare '150 miles' here is ambiguous against both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is cut off mid-clause ('provided that such other destination is at a location further') — the condition is simply missing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D(iv) lists Hightstown as a transfer point 'in use as of the date of signing', which contradicts this elimination of the Hightstown point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, concrete conversion obligation with a fixed deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Farer and Hightstown items and with 22-D's direct-run principle.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It operates by amending a phrase on a page of a superseded 1973–75 booklet, which is unintelligible without that external document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D(ix) already states the 27-mile run-time rule in the present text, making this amendment redundant or, if the booklet differs, conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixed run time and off-day options, though 'within 60 days of the ratification' is stale and 'mutually agreeable' softens the deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D(ix)'s 27-miles-per-hour rule would generate a different run time for Philadelphia than the flat nine hours fixed here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete tax-withholding and voucher obligations with a 24-hour deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A Times side letter confirms continuation of separate vacation checks and 20-F addresses paycheck errors; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Kicked off in variables of five' and 'as heretofore' are trade shorthand with no defined content in the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-B gives the Publisher the right to determine the manner of wrapping and tying, which this shop-specific rule narrows.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short jurisdictional statement over a defined operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2-A.1's inclusion of airway terminal routing and 2-D.1's recognition of air terminals as delivery points.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement merely to 'observe ... to determine manpower requirements' creates no obligation and no decision rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-C requires new mechanical devices to be operated exclusively by unit employees, so an open-ended manpower study sits against that entitlement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise relief minutes for each vehicle type; 'or part thereof' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's truck-loader entry states the same relief periods, so the provision is duplicated in two places within Section 22.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Disputes go to a single named individual with no successor mechanism should he be unavailable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16 makes the Joint Standing Committee and Appeals Board the route for all interpretation disputes, so this personal referral is a direct departure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Until they are in force Section 2-E.2 as written will continue to apply' leaves the date and mechanism by which the decisions come into force unstated, and 'status quo ... maintained in all details' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly an interpretation of 2-E.2 for The Times only, so the same paragraph bears two meanings depending on the Publisher — a coherence problem for a single agreement.
